notes: Scope: six facility rows, each placed in a named city by a page I opened and carrying a DOE or LPO award. Facility statuses are my reading of the cited page; none of the six pages stated a current construction status, so the statuses are not verified against 2026 news.
MP Materials Fort Worth (DoD award) was skipped: /research/minerals.json already has 'MP Materials Independence facility, Fort Worth'.

Albemarle: the release says 'nearly $150 million' DOE. The $149.7M figure and 'Ongoing, end date March 31, 2027' come from a search summary of the DOE award database (not opened). A March 2026 DOE environmental assessment (search summary, not opened) describes continuing about $149 million federal cost-share. Albemarle's separate $90 million DoD award for Kings Mountain (search summary; a release titled 'albemarle receives 90 million critical materials award department defense boost us lithium' appeared in results) was NOT opened and is not in the rows. The 'Kings Mountain, North Carolina, location' sentence is from the release and is the location quote.

Syrah: the $220M grant location quote is 'for the expansion of its Vidalia active anode material (AAM) facility in Louisiana.' (NS Energy, Oct. 21, 2022). Separately, DOE's LPO closed a $102.1 million loan to Syrah Technologies for the Syrah Vidalia Facility in Louisiana (batteryindustry.net, quote: 'has closed a $102.1-million loan to Australia-based Syrah Technologies LLC.', dated 29 July 2022). The loan is not a second row. The grant's binding agreement was still pending at the time of the Oct 2022 article, and a 2026 status was not verified. A $350 million ATVM loan request is reported by a mining.com search summary, not opened and not in the rows.

Novonix: the award was reduced from the $150 million selected in Oct 2022 to $100 million and reallocated to the Riverside facility in Chattanooga, targeting 20,000 tpa (search summary; the finalized release says the Riverside facility doubles capacity to 20,000 tpa). The release's location sentence is 'in Chattanooga, Tennessee.' A separate $754.8 million DOE conditional loan for a Chattanooga synthetic graphite facility (search summary, not opened, year not confirmed) is not in the rows.

Redwood Materials (McCarran, NV): the DOE/LPO conditional commitment of up to $2 billion (ATVM program) is confirmed from the Canary Media article. Canary spells the site 'McCarren'. The page's location quote is 'The loan will help Redwood Materials build its $3.5 billion McCarren, Nevada factory' ($3.5B is the page's total project figure, not the loan). The energy.gov LPO page returned 404 and was not read, so the conditional-commitment date is taken from Canary's Feb 9, 2023 article date. Jobs (about 1,600 permanent) are from a search summary, not opened. The loan's closing or disbursement status is not verified.

Piedmont Lithium (Tennessee lithium hydroxide plant) NOT PLACED in a city. DOE selected a $141.7 million grant for the Tennessee project (Business Wire, Oct 19, 2022 and Kitco), but the Business Wire page returned 403 and the Kitco page does not name a town. The Canadian Mining Journal page says '265 km southeast of Nashville' and names no town. The Process Worldwide permit article (July 31, 2023) gives the plant as 'the Company's proposed Tennessee Lithium project in McMinn County, Tennessee, USA', and names Etowah only for an office ('supporting the revitalization efforts of downtown Etowah, Tennessee'). The grant also appears in search summaries as Etowah, McMinn County, but no opened page states the plant at Etowah. Recommend a row with county-level location (McMinn County, TN) once a city-level page is opened, or the Piedmont/Elevra 10-K.

Li-Cycle Rochester Hub (DOE LPO loan up to $475 million: $445M principal plus $30M capitalized interest, per Fastmarkets). The Fastmarkets quote is 'The loan of up to $475 million includes up to $445 million of principal and up to $30 million in capitalized interest', dated Nov. 12, 2024. The page names the 'Rochester Hub Project' but does not state 'Rochester, New York' in a sentence, and the esgnews and battery-tech pages returned 403 and 404. Not placed; a row needs a page with 'Rochester, New York'.

American Battery Technology Company (ABTC): the Nov. 17, 2022 release (SEC 8-K exhibit) gives a $10M additional competitive DOE grant under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law for 'its unconventional, sedimentary claystone resource near Tonopah, Nev.' That is a resource project, not a plant with a stated city, so it is not a facility row. A $144M contracted DOE recycling award (search summary) is reported at both McCarran and Fernley, NV, with conflicting locations, so no row was made. The $57M Tonopah lithium hydroxide award and the $144M recycling award were NOT opened.

Nth Cycle: NOT PLACED. The Waste Dive article states Nth Cycle was awarded up to $100 million in the Aug. 20, 2026 DOE round, but says 'the facility will open somewhere in the Southeast by 2029 but has not announced an exact location.' The Fairfield, Ohio facility, which began operations in 2024, is an existing operation and not the DOE-funded site.

Princeton NuEnergy: the Waste Dive article gives 'up to $50 million' DOE and a '$110 million facility in Commerce, Georgia'. The brief's 'Chester SC?' guess is not supported by any page I read. Product not stated on the fetched article (black mass processing is inferred and not quoted).

Not checked within budget: Coreshell, Clarios, Li Industries (one search returned only Blue Whale; these names were not searched separately). Thacker Pass (Lithium Americas, LPO $2.26B): not searched, so no city is claimed. Nickel awardees (Talon) skipped per brief.

Blue Whale Materials: the award is for expanding the Bartlesville, Oklahoma lithium-ion battery recycling plant. Search summaries (not opened) describe a $110 million four-year project and a 2025 baseline plant commissioning. The row's status is 'expansion' and is my reading, not a verified current status.
